key_insight: Porous coating changes water-exit behavior in two opposing ways: it suppresses free-surface rise while often strengthening and restructuring the submerged wake, with the strongest pressure deficits seen for higher-pore-density foam in several conditions.
engineering_relevance: Adding a porous outer layer can be used as a passive design strategy to reduce splash/free-surface disturbance during water exit, but the wake and pressure loads must be re-evaluated because they may intensify rather than simply weaken.
method: Experiments on circular cylinders with a 30 mm solid core and 10 mm porous foam layer at 10, 20, and 60 PPI, compared with a smooth cylinder
Time-resolved particle image velocimetry to measure wake evolution and reconstruct pressure fields
Proper orthogonal decomposition to quantify how many modes capture 95% of the wake energy
evidence_signal: Across Re = 1.50×10^4 to 5.00×10^4 and Fr = 0.37 to 4.08, porous cylinders reduced free-surface elevation, while 20 PPI required only 9–10 POD modes and 9–18 modes were enough to recover 95% of modal energy overall.
watch_item: The beneficial reduction in free-surface response does not guarantee lower hydrodynamic loading, since the porous cases can produce larger circulation, vortex area, and pressure deficits depending on pore density and operating condition.
paper_title: Effect of Porous Coating on the Water-Exit Dynamics of a Circular Cylinder
